Looking at the folds: the first fold (vertical) maps the right half onto the left half, the second fold (horizontal) maps the bottom onto the top, and the third fold (along the diagonal from the center to the top‑left vertex) produces the triangle whose corners are: the center of the octagon (bottom right), a "axis" vertex corner (top right), and a "diagonal" vertex corner (left point).

The cut removes the left point of the triangle. Tracing the layers, that corner contains all four diagonal vertices of the octagon (NE, NW, SE, SW). Cutting it off therefore removes a V‑shaped notch at each diagonal vertex, while the top, bottom, left, and right vertices remain intact as points.

Unfolding gives an octagon with four notches at the diagonal positions — picture D.
